[Linux Mint]

After searching for about 2 days, I found a fix that works for my particular sound setup to eliminate crackling audio with multiple sound sources (i.e.: playing games, listening to music and voice chatting at the same time).

Your setup might require different values, but for most modern hardware these will probably be a good start.

sudo gedit /etc/pulse/daemon.conf

Lines 82 and 83:

default-fragments = 5 (default 4)

default-fragment-size-msec = 4 (default 25)
[Solved] Crackling sound via USB audio devices
Never had this problem myself, but I shall file this away as something to try, should I ever encounter it. :)
I never had an issue with usb audio... without pulse.

As a followup, I've done some experimenting with the values. 8 fragments of 10 msec each has resulted in much clearer sound, even in cases where I can consistently replicate sound crackling (alt-tabbing from Enter the Gungeon).
Followup to the followup, someone's already solved this on the LinuxMint forums. Apparently there's math behind it and everything.

Seedlings for my Juice Planters! Step-by-step description in comments.

Today I buried a bunch of plant-babies in small dirt cups. Here's how it went:

  • Start with a bunch of dirt cups.

These were actually used once before, but the seeds that grew were small and weak. We ripped their bodies out of the dirt cups to make room for new, worthier plant-babies. Who said gardening isn't metal as fuck?

  • Use a plastic tray to hold them.

I suppose you could hold them in your hands, but that gets boring fast. The plastic grid also has little lips that I think tell you how much water you should put in there. Our cats do not approve.

  • Set out what kind of seed-babies you want in your dirt cups.

I chose Tomatillos, Jalapenos, Bell Peppers and Roma tomatoes because I'm all about the salsa. Poblano peppers because chile rellenos are amazing, then some weird mutant yellow tomatoes because they looked fun. As we will later learn, I am an excellent planner.

  • Pulverize the dirt so your plant-babies can rip out of it easier.

All my seeds were supposed to be planted at 5mm, which I took to mean these seeds are rubbish at pushing up through the dirt and I 'fluffed' the cups with a toothpick to make that happen. Last season we had many plants end up stunted because I packed my dirt too tightly and their roots couldn't get through it.

  • Plant-babies are extremely small. Insert as required.

These seeds are more like wafers - the tomato seeds were even smaller! No wonder they have trouble getting through the soil.

  • Instructions unclear, seeds now stuck in penis.

I put three in each dirt cup, giving me a total of ~12 seeds for each type. Since I'm planting late in the season, that should be enough to guarantee I get at least a few candidates for the hanging planters. If I end up with a surplus of seedlings I'll be cutting more juice boxes!

  • Realize you have miscalculated.

My tray holds 4x5 dirt cups. I have six seed types. This happened even after I counted things off earlier! Sheesh, good thing I'm not a roofer.

  • Fill two more cups with plant-baby food.

Ah yes, dirt - that's the word I was looking for. Again, I pull some used stuff from the actual gardener on our farm. Most of what I'm doing is just bumble-fucking through the motions of following her around! But having planter cups and dirt around is always handy, and she's happy to offer me advice even if she thinks my hanging juice planters are the ugliest things ever.

  • Moisturize the dirt cups!

Seeds don't grow when they're dry. So getting them the opposite of dry must be a good way to start things moving! Pouring water on top of the soil quickly causes it to compact, so instead I poured water into the trays and let the dirt soak it up like a sponge. Those dirt cups soak up a LOT of water, by the way.

  • Place your plant-baby tray in with all the others.

I put the tray in our cheap little $20 plastic greenhouse with all the seedlings my garden mentor has already started - also pictured is our 4-year-old garden guardian, destroyer of slugs and poker of snakes.
Great work! I'm really looking forward to seeing some awesome plants, hope it all works out. Sweet kid, btw. I can't wait until my little man can help me garden.

Thanks! She's an awesome kid, tough as nails. She's already killed a snake this spring!

Hanging planter was awesome last summer for letting the kiddo pick cherry tomatoes - in fact that's a big reason why I'm expanding from 1 to 6 planters this season.
